title: The Serpent
world_rule: Setting rule for Genesis 2-3 (Eden): a lush untouched garden with nothing made by people: no buildings, walls, tents, roads, paths, fences or tools.

Because you have listened to your wife’s voice, and have eaten from the tree, about which I commanded you, saying, ‘You shall not eat of it,’ the ground is cursed for your sake.

moral.heading: What This Story Teaches
moral.paragraph: The serpent did not force the woman; he questioned what God had said and then denied it: “You won’t really die” (Genesis 3:4). The New Testament warns about the same danger, “as the serpent deceived Eve in his craftiness” (2 Corinthians 11:3). Sin started with wanting what God had forbidden, just as James describes: “each one is tempted when he is drawn away by his own lust and enticed” (James 1:14). Afterward the man and woman hid and blamed others. The Bible later explains that through one man “sin entered into the world” (Romans 5:12). Yet the chapter does not end in silence: God still spoke to them, and he made them garments of skins and clothed them (Genesis 3:21).
